newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends below US$0.6900, tracks Aust. dlr.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends below US$0.6900, tracks Aust. dlr.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended just below US$0.6900 on Monday after a quiet session, the currency being influenced by a slightly softer Australian dollar.
"The market got itself caught a little long first up and drifted off with the Aussie. That, and selling out of the States, basically pushed the Kiwi lower," said one dealer.
The market was turning its attention to jobs data on Tuesday, which economists expect to put unemployment at 6.15 percent over the March quarter, up from 5.9 percent in the December quarter.
The risk was seen as remaining on the downside for the Kiwi and rallies were expected to be sold into.
The currency finished at US$0.6892/99 from its 0.6903/10 opening, having traded a 0.6889-12 range on the day while the Trade-Weighted Index finished at 68.48 from 68.61 at the open.
The Australian dollar finished locally at US$0.7822/27 from 0.7831/36 in late Sydney trade on Friday.
